title: 로마자 보고 한글로 쓰기: 김밥, 커피, 학교
objective: By the end, you can read a romanized word such as "hakgyo" or "gimbap", write it in correct Hangul, and say it aloud.
summary: Learn to turn romanized Korean words, like those on menus and signs, back into correct Hangul.

task.title: Write it in Hangul
task.line: Read each romanized word, write it in Hangul, then say it aloud.

letters.sound: Two Roman letters make one Korean vowel: eo [ㅓ], eu [ㅡ].
letters.as: ㅓ: like 'u' in 'cup'. ㅡ: say 'oo' with your lips spread flat, as in a smile.

letters.letter: g → ㄱ, k (end of syllable) → ㄱ, k (before a vowel) → ㅋ
letters.sound: g is ㄱ. k at the end of a syllable is also ㄱ [k].
letters.as: k before a vowel is ㅋ, a strong 'k' with a puff of air.

letters.sound: ng at the end is ㅇ [ŋ]. A syllable that starts with a vowel also begins with a silent ㅇ.
hangugeo [한구거] is written 한국어: the final ㄱ moves over to the next syllable.
letters.as: Write the real word you know, not every syllable you hear.

exercises: Write in Hangul. Two Roman letters can make one vowel: ① eomma ② geurim ③ uyu
Write in Hangul. k before a vowel is ㅋ, and k at the end is ㄱ: ① keopi ② kong ③ sikdang
Write in Hangul. Use ㅇ for ng at the end and for a syllable that starts with a vowel: ① gang ② oi ③ sarang
Choose the correct spelling for the romanization: ① eumak 'music' (음악 / 은악) ② gabang (가방 / 거방) ③ oneul (오늘 / 우늘)
You see these words on a restaurant menu. Write them in Hangul: ① gimbap ② bibimbap ③ bulgogi
answers: ① 엄마 ② 그림 ③ 우유
① 커피 ② 콩 ③ 식당
① 강 ② 오이 ③ 사랑
① 음악 ② 가방 ③ 오늘
① 김밥 ② 비빔밥 ③ 불고기
